glosses: To follow as a model or a pattern; to make a copy, counterpart or semblance of.

examples.text: Another bird quickly learned to imitate the song of a canary that was mated with it, but as the parrakeet improved in the performance the canary degenerated, and came at last to mingle the other bird's harsh chitterings with its own proper music.
The room was dark and cool, lit with a dim red light. “This was designed to imitate a cave,” said Rosas.

glosses: One who imitates or plagiarizes others' work.

examples.text: And in it all they are merely copy-cats—servile followers of the aristocratic creed, but without the genuine prestige of the old-time nobilities.

glosses: A criminal who imitates the crimes of another; specifically, a criminal who commits the same crime, especially a highly-publicized one, that has just or recently been committed by someone else.

examples.text: a copycat strangler

glosses: To act as a copycat; to copy in a shameless or derivative way.

examples.text: Because beasts don't talk with words, they talk with sounds, and I copycatted my language from beasts and birds[…]

glosses: Saupoudrer de farine des éléments que l’on a préalablement fait revenir dans de la matière grasse, farine que l’on laisse cuire légèrement avant de verser dessus un liquide de mouillement (lait, eau, bouillon) afin d’obtenir une sauce liée.

examples.text: Sauce à la Sainte-Menehould. — Mettez dans une casserole un morceau de beurre coupé, singez-le de farine; délayez votre sauce avec du lait ou de la crème; […].
Découper la volaille. Faire sauter les morceaux sans leur laisser prendre couleur. Singer et mouiller avec un petit verre de vin blanc sec et du bouillon de veau.
